category_title: Struggling readers who ask relevant questions to discontinue reading
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are doing a shared reading of 'Where the wild things are', and it is the student's turn to read from the new text.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the next page of 'Where the wild things are'. It is your turn to read.

STUDENT: (Switches gaze directly to the text)

TUTOR: Go ahead and start.

STUDENT: stepped into his private...

TUTOR: What is the next word?

STUDENT: Why's it private?

options.A: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) at the end of each shared reading session.
options.B: Allow the student to select a book from several choices and use a constructivist approach to mediation, implementing scaffolds focused on meaning and comprehension.
options.C: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the characters, setting, or plot.
options.D: Ask follow-up questions about the text to model conversational skills during the shared reading sessions.
